Looking at the folded packet: the dashed edges (left and bottom) are the fold creases (the center lines of the square), while the solid edges (top and right) are the original outer edges.

**Analyzing each cut:**
- **Triangle at the top‑right corner** (where the two open/original edges meet): this corner corresponds to all four corners of the full sheet, so unfolding produces **chamfered (cut) corners at all four corners**.
- **Rectangular notch on the left edge** (a fold crease): unfolding across the vertical crease makes a full rectangular hole centered on the vertical midline; unfolding across the horizontal crease duplicates it below. Result: **two rectangles on the vertical center line**, one above and one below the center.
- **Triangle at the bottom‑left corner** (where the two creases meet = center of sheet): unfolding across both creases reflects this triangle four times, forming a **diamond hole at the center**.

**Checking options:**
- A: only top corners cut, triangle instead of diamond — wrong.
- B: center hole is a square, not a diamond — wrong.
- C: four off-center squares instead of two rectangles on the midline — wrong.
- D: corners are not cut — wrong.
- E: all four corners chamfered, diamond at center, two rectangles on the vertical midline — matches.

\boxed{E}
